signals.headline: Alberta Data Centres Have Asked for 26,849 MW, More Than Double the Province’s Record Peak
signals.theFact: Data centre developers had asked to connect 26,849 MW of new load to Alberta’s grid by October, more than double the province’s all-time peak demand of 12,785 MW, and AESO’s entire 1,200 MW interim limit went to just two projects. The Circuit’s four-province comparison finds Alberta, Quebec, Ontario and B.C. all now rationing or repricing data centre power, with B.C. capping new data centre supply at 400 MW over two years and no public list yet of who won it.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls targets sub-10 MW brownfield sites that stay outside B.C.’s ≥10 MW competitive call and connect through BC Hydro’s standard process, instead of joining a multi-gigawatt queue for rationed power.

signals.headline: Sherbrooke Delays a Data Centre Freeze as 12,000 Sign Against a 96 MW Campus
signals.theFact: Sherbrooke Mayor Marie-Claude Bibeau kept a proposed data centre moratorium off Tuesday’s council agenda, saying the city needs more time to weigh its legal and technical impacts. Residents are fighting a 96 MW project by U.S.-backed Keel Infrastructure on land the city conditionally sold in August, with a petition against the sale topping 12,000 signatures and two more crypto-to-AI conversions in the works.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls keeps each site under 10 MW on already-zoned brownfield industrial land, a footprint small enough to avoid the scale that turns a municipal land sale into a 12,000-signature fight.

signals.headline: Budget 2026 Promises Canadian AI Firms 500 MW of Sovereign Compute, With No Sites or Timeline Yet
signals.theFact: Budget 2026 commits Ottawa to help Canadian AI companies access 500 MW of sovereign computing capacity through backstops and offtake agreements, after finding that large tech firms are locking up new Canadian capacity with long-term contracts. DataCentre.ca notes the measure does not identify participating facilities, a delivery schedule, or the value of the financial support.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Canadian organizations that need sovereign inference now don’t have to wait for program rules: Ocean Falls’ MicroNode puts Canadian-controlled AI compute directly behind their own firewall in British Columbia.

signals.headline: SCOR’s CEO: Insurers Can Assemble About US$15B per Risk, but AI Campuses Now Carry up to US$50B
signals.theFact: SCOR group CEO Thierry Léger told the Singapore International Reinsurance Conference on November 2 that the industry can assemble only around US$15 billion of capacity per risk, while a Howden report estimates single hyperscale AI campuses can carry insurable values of up to US$50 billion. He warned that AI and data centre exposures are growing faster than reinsurers can build the capability to price them.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls’ distributed sub-10 MW sites stay well inside what the market can absorb, and its AI Infrastructure Captive Program covers the AI infrastructure risks traditional insurers won’t take.

signals.headline: BC Hydro’s Data Centre Power Picks Are Still Pending, and the Okanagan Is Shut Out
signals.theFact: BC Hydro has still not announced which of the nearly 800 MW of data centre applications will share its 400 MW allocation, after results expected in September were postponed by the provincial election. iNFOnews reports the call excludes FortisBC service areas, which cover much of the Okanagan and are already nearing power capacity, and that the province has restricted BC Hydro from supplying extra power to wholesalers like FortisBC for new data centres.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls targets sub-10 MW brownfield sites that sit outside the ≥10 MW competitive call, so projects can move through BC Hydro’s standard interconnection process instead of waiting on a rationed, delayed allocation.

signals.headline: Memphis Splits 6–6 on a Data Centre Moratorium, Then Bans Evaporative Cooling
signals.theFact: Memphis City Council denied a 12-month moratorium on new data centres on a 6–6 vote, at a meeting that drew more residents than the 407 allowed inside the chambers. The council instead passed an ordinance for large-scale data centres that prohibits routine evaporative and once-through cooling, requires closed-loop water circulation, and bars major withdrawals of local water for cooling.
signals.oceanFallsAngle: Ocean Falls places closed-loop or air-cooled sub-10 MW MicroClusters on already-zoned brownfield industrial land, the small, low-water footprint that rules like these are pushing the industry toward.
